coupling: lib/parsedate.c defines a direct-indexed table `tzone[]` (one int16_t per single-letter time zone A-Z, indexed as tzone[first-'A']) plus a guard that rejects anything outside 'A'..'Z' or equal to 'J'. Commit 2f16799 (the original 'faster lookups' refactor) shrinks the table by one entry, dropping the trailing 'Z' (Zulu/UTC) slot, and compensates with a short-circuit `if(check[0]=='Z') return 0;` placed before the table read, inside the very same commit. Read alone, 2f16799 is internally self-consistent and correct: the 25-entry table and the explicit Z special case together cover exactly 'A'..'Z' and this specific commit's own new unit test (unit4781, added in this same commit, which checks every single letter A-Z including 'Z'->0) passes. Commit 8ba2eaa (the following day's 'store as uint32/less memory' refactor) mechanically converts tzone from the struct-with-name form to a bare int16_t array and simplifies the single-letter branch back to a direct `tzone[first-'A']` lookup -- which is exactly upstream's real, idiomatic one-line form for this lookup. Read alone, against the tree state 8ba2eaa is actually based on, this also looks like an unremarkable, faithful representation-conversion commit: the array it carries forward already has however many entries 2f16799 left it with, and collapsing a single-letter dispatch down to a plain array index is the obvious simplification once the struct/name fields are gone. Neither diff, by itself, contains anything a commit-by-commit reviewer would flag: 2f16799 is a correct, if non-obvious, size optimization (you must hand-verify that dropping the table's last row is covered by the new early return placed earlier in the same function); 8ba2eaa is a correct-looking mechanical refactor (you must separately hand-count that the carried-over array actually still has a slot for every letter the unchanged guard admits, which requires reasoning about the array as it was left by a different, earlier commit, not anything visible in 8ba2eaa's own diff). Only by holding both commits in mind at once -- '2f16799 removed the table row but added a compensating special case' and '8ba2eaa removed that special case while carrying the table forward at its reduced size' -- does the gap appear: for input 'Z', `first-'A'` is 25 but tzone[] (after 8ba2eaa) has only 25 elements (indices 0-24, covering A-Y), so the lookup reads exactly one int16_t past the end of the global array. Fixing only 2f16799 (e.g. restoring the 26th/Z row there) or only 8ba2eaa (e.g. re-adding the Z special case there) independently closes the gap; the point is that neither commit's diff, inspected on its own, surfaces anything to fix -- the composition is what is broken, and the reachable date formats/letters used by every other single-letter, two-letter, three-letter and four-letter zone are completely unaffected (unit4781's non-Z cases, and all of checkday/checkmonth/tzthree/tzfoura, are untouched and still pass).
